players.product: multimodal clinical data, diagnostics, and AI applications

quarterly_data.signal: Revenue increased 22% to $382.5 million in the first quarter lapping a fully integrated Ambry. Diagnostics revenue was $289.3 million, up 20% year over year, as slower hereditary growth was offset by accelerating CGP testing; hereditary revenue was up 5% to $107.4 million. Data and Apps revenue was $93.2 million, up 28%, with the Insights data licensing and modeling business growing 36%.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $382.5M (+22%); Diagnostics $289.3M (+20%); hereditary $107.4M (+5%); Data and Apps $93.2M (+28%); Insights +36%

quarterly_data.signal: The solid tumor algorithm attach rate was 45% in Q2, a slight uptick from the 40% quoted in Q1, and core volume growth accelerated to 31%; management noted many of those algorithms remain unpaid, so they carry no revenue impact today but help drive core volume. In minimal residual disease, where only about 10% of the sales force sells the test, volumes ran approximately 6,500 tests in Q1 and approximately 9,000 tests in Q2, growing 38% quarter-over-quarter. On July 20 Tempus announced an agreement to acquire Personalis in a 100% stock transaction with an option to elect cash capped at 50% of consideration, targeting a market management sized at more than $20 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: algorithm attach rate 45% (from 40% in Q1); core volume growth 31%; ~9,000 MRD tests in Q2 (+38% QoQ) vs ~6,500 in Q1; >$20B MRD market

quarterly_data.signal: GAAP net income was $5.6 million and adjusted EBITDA was $8 million, a $13.6 million year-over-year improvement, while cash used in operating activities improved to negative $7.5 million. Cash, equivalents and marketable securities ended at $820.7 million versus $643.8 million last quarter after a $460 million offering of 0.0% convertible senior notes due 2032 that repaid an Ares Capital loan and saves over $30 million annually in interest, enabling positive free cash flow by year-end.
quarterly_data.figure: net income $5.6M; adjusted EBITDA $8M (+$13.6M YoY); operating cash flow -$7.5M; cash $820.7M vs $643.8M; $460M convertible notes; >$30M annual interest savings

quarterly_data.signal: Tempus received FDA approval for tumor-only xT CDx, allowing the entire solid tumor DNA portfolio to migrate to unified ADLT pricing for an estimated $200 uplift in ASP, approximately $85 million on an annual basis beginning in 2027. The xF liquid biopsy is in front of the FDA now, with approval expected in the latter half of 2027 at an assumed $7,500 ADLT price for an incremental $550 of ASP; between the two approvals management anticipates approximately $400 million of revenue uplift in 2028.
quarterly_data.figure: $200 ASP uplift (~$85M annually from 2027); xF incremental $550 ASP at assumed $7,500 ADLT price; ~$400M revenue uplift in 2028

quarterly_data.signal: Management said a large multi-year data licensing and modeling agreement was signed with BioNTech, which now joins the ranks of AstraZeneca, GlaxoSmithKline, Bristol Myers Squibb and others, alongside large deals with Daiichi Sankyo, LevelSet Bio and Incyte Pharmaceuticals. Together these contributed to approximately $200 million in total bookings in the quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: ~$200 million in total bookings in the quarter

quarterly_data.signal: Tempus delivered the first version of its multimodal foundation model to AstraZeneca and is now working on the next version; the model was used to predict which patients responded in several public and blinded clinical trials. Management described the data business as having its best run of momentum in years, with customers wanting not just data but access to Lens, provisioned GPUs inside Lens and models that are built and kept in the Tempus environment, supporting a long-term data growth ambition in the close to 30% range plus.
quarterly_data.figure: first foundation model version delivered; long-term data growth target close to 30% range plus

quarterly_data.signal: Full-year 2026 guidance was increased to $1.595 billion-$1.605 billion, representing approximately 25% growth, with 2026 adjusted EBITDA of approximately $65 million, an improvement of about $72 million over 2025. Management said it intends to see continued improvement in adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow in 2027 even with the Personalis acquisition.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 revenue $1.595B-$1.605B (~25% growth); adjusted EBITDA ~$65M (+~$72M vs 2025)

connects_to.relationship: multimodal foundation model delivery and data licensing

contracts.signal: Tempus introduced initial results from and successfully delivered the first version of its foundation model to AstraZeneca, which accepted it after the model met acceptance criteria, performing as well as highly tuned internal models from both companies when predicting response in public and blinded trials. Management added that AstraZeneca is also a licensee of Tempus data and products under an agreement with several years left to run, with projects already committed that extend into 2027.
contracts.units: first version of the multimodal foundation model delivered and accepted
contracts.date_signed: not stated; existing agreement described as having several years left
contracts.type: foundation model development and data licensing

contracts.signal: Management named Bristol Myers Squibb among the pharma companies already holding large Tempus data licensing and modeling agreements, saying the newly signed multi-year BioNTech agreement joins the ranks of AstraZeneca, GlaxoSmithKline, Bristol Myers Squibb and others as evidence that Tempus data and modeling capabilities are becoming instrumental to pharma.
contracts.units: large data licensing and modeling agreement
